wizStep.label: Page
wizStep.help: Only the pages that fit your answers are listed. Missing something? Change "What do you want to use?" or "What do you have?".

options.label: What do you want to use?
Alarm system: switching on and off

w0t.text: This assistant guides you through the setup page by page. First you say what you want to use and what you already have – after that you only get the pages that fit. At the end everything is checked and you save with "Save" at the bottom of the page. All answers are the normal settings of the adapter – you can come back here at any time.

w0a.text: Do you want to use the assistant?

w0at.text: Yes: simply go on with "Next" at the bottom.

wizDone.label: No – I know ioBroker and set it up myself: show all settings now
wizDone.help: All tabs appear at once. The assistant stays here and can be used at any time.

w0skip.text: All tabs are shown – choose them at the top. Do not forget "Save" at the bottom.

w0g2.text: State: one single value in ioBroker, e.g. "kitchen window open" or "living room lamp on". You pick it with the button next to the field from the object list. Function: a group of states in ioBroker (Objects → Enumerations → Functions), e.g. "Windows" with all window contacts. If you have no such groups, simply put the devices into the tables "by hand".

w1h.text: What do you want to use?

w1t.text: Tick what you want. Only the pages for it follow – everything else is skipped. You can change it later at any time.

alarmEnabled.label: I want to use the alarm system
alarmEnabled.help: Monitors doors, windows and motion detectors. When armed, an open door or a movement raises an alarm: message, lamps, siren.

simEnabled.label: When we are away: switch light and TV as if somebody were at home (presence simulation)
simEnabled.help: While you are away, lamps and devices such as the TV are switched as if somebody were at home – learned from your own habits.

w1com.text: Comfort functions – for you at home

eveningLight.label: In the evening, switch lamps on and off by themselves at our times (evening light)
eveningLight.help: Lamps on at dusk and off at bedtime, so you do not have to think of it. Runs every evening – when you are away, the simulation comes on top.

morningLight.label: In the morning, switch lamps on and off by themselves at our times (morning light)
morningLight.help: Lamps on at wake-up time and off as soon as it is light – only on dark mornings. Runs every morning, also when you are away.

w1n.text: Nothing ticked yet – tick at least one part to go on.

w2t.text: Let Home Guard look first: "Search automatically" looks through your ioBroker (functions, door lock, messenger, speaker, brightness sensor) and fills in what fits – only empty fields, it takes about 15 seconds. Then check the ticks below and correct them. Every tick decides which pages follow – what you do not have is not asked at all.

w2any.text: Any kind of device works – what counts is only whether it should raise an alarm from outside, inside or always.

wizHasDoors.label: Door and window contacts, glass break or vibration detectors

wizHasDoorsOk.text: ✔ Door and window contacts, glass break or vibration detectors – already set up

wizHasMotion.label: Motion detectors or other detectors inside (presence sensor, light barrier, camera with motion detection …)

wizHasMotionOk.text: ✔ Motion detectors or other detectors inside (presence sensor, light barrier, camera with motion detection …) – already set up

wizHasFire.label: Smoke, heat, water or gas detectors, or a panic button

wizHasFireOk.text: ✔ Smoke, heat, water or gas detectors, or a panic button – already set up

wizHasReport.label: Sensors that should only report, e.g. garden gate, letter box or doorbell

wizHasReportOk.text: ✔ Sensors that should only report, e.g. garden gate, letter box or doorbell – already set up

wizHasSiren.label: A siren (or a socket with a horn)

wizHasSirenOk.text: ✔ A siren (or a socket with a horn) – already set up

lockEnabled.label: A smart door lock (e.g. Nuki) – unlocking switches the alarm system off

presenceEnabled.label: ioBroker knows who is at home (phone in the Wi-Fi, GPS …)

wizHasSpeaker.label: A speaker that reads texts aloud (e.g. Alexa)

wizHasSpeakerOk.text: ✔ A speaker that reads texts aloud (e.g. Alexa) – already set up

wizHasAlexa.label: Amazon Echo (Alexa) – for the alarm or radio in the simulation

wizHasAlexaOk.text: ✔ Amazon Echo (Alexa) – for the alarm or radio in the simulation – already set up

wizHasLuxOk.text: ✔ An outdoor brightness sensor – already set up

wizHasDevices.label: A TV, radio or similar that should also run during the simulation

wizHasDevicesOk.text: ✔ A TV, radio or similar that should also run during the simulation – already set up

wskip3.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w11t.text: For each person you need a state that is true while they are at home – e.g. from the adapters ping, iCloud or Life360. Take them from a function (e.g. "Presence") or put them into the table. Several states of one person (e.g. GPS and Wi-Fi) get the same name in the column "Person" – the person counts as at home when one of them says so.

w11s.text: The search on the page "What do you have?" may already have filled this in.

wskip4.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w3t.text: Armed / disarmed: the alarm system is switched on / off. There are three ways of being armed: Full protection – nobody is at home, doors, windows and motion detectors are watched. Perimeter protection – you are at home, only doors and windows are watched, you can move around freely inside. Night protection – like perimeter protection, but switched on by itself at night.

w3n.text: On the next pages: which sensors are watched → single sensors and exceptions → times → switching on and off → messages → what happens on an alarm.

wskip5.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w4h.text: Outer skin: doors, windows, glass break …

w4t.text: Everything that reports a break-in from outside: door and window contacts, window handles, glass break, vibration or roller shutter sensors. They raise an alarm in every way of being armed – full, perimeter and night protection. Any state works – it raises the alarm as soon as it reports true, a number above 0 or "open". The easiest way is a function – everything in it is watched, and sensors you add to it later are picked up by themselves.

w4tx.text: Exception: doors and windows with the tick "ignore at home" are only watched in full protection (see below).

w4tb.text: Single devices without a function, and exceptions, come in on the page "Single sensors & exceptions".

w4s.text: The search on the page "What do you have?" may already have filled this in.

autoPerimeter.label: Take these sensors from a function

w4ih.text: Doors and windows you open while at home

w4it.text: E.g. the bedroom window you tilt at night: add it on the page "Single sensors & exceptions" and tick "ignore at home". It stays watched in full protection (nobody at home) and is ignored in perimeter and night protection.

wskip6.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w5t.text: Detectors inside the house: motion and presence sensors, light barriers, a camera with motion detection, an interior door. Only watched in full protection, i.e. when nobody is at home. Any state works – it raises the alarm as soon as it reports true, a number above 0 or "open". The easiest way is a function – everything in it is watched, and sensors you add to it later are picked up by themselves.

w5tb.text: Single devices without a function, and exceptions, come in on the page "Single sensors & exceptions".

w5s.text: The search on the page "What do you have?" may already have filled this in.

autoFull.label: Take these detectors from a function

wskip7.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w6t.text: Smoke, heat, water, gas or CO detectors – and a panic button. They are always active, also when the alarm system is off. Choose whether they only send a message, also speak, or raise a full alarm with siren; a panic button belongs on "full alarm" (single devices get their own reaction on the page "Single sensors & exceptions"). Any state works – it raises the alarm as soon as it reports true, a number above 0 or "open". The easiest way is a function – everything in it is watched, and sensors you add to it later are picked up by themselves.

w6tb.text: Single devices without a function, and exceptions, come in on the page "Single sensors & exceptions".

w6s.text: The search on the page "What do you have?" may already have filled this in.

autoFire.label: Take the detectors from a function

hazardDefault.label: Reaction of the danger detectors of the function

wskip8.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w7t.text: Never an alarm – just a message, e.g. "garden gate opened", "post in the letter box" or "somebody rang". The easiest way is a function – everything in it is watched, and sensors you add to it later are picked up by themselves.

w7tb.text: Single devices without a function, and exceptions, come in on the page "Single sensors & exceptions".

w7s.text: The search on the page "What do you have?" may already have filled this in.

autoReport.label: Take these sensors from a function

wskip9.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w8t.text: Important: when you come home, opening the front door would raise the alarm at once. So add a row for the door you come in through and tick "delayed" – then you have the entry delay to switch the alarm system off.

w8l.text: Your door lock switches the alarm system off when you unlock it – then "delayed" is not needed.

w8t2.text: The table is for four things: 1. a device that is in no function – add a row with the area it belongs to. 2. a device from a function that should behave differently (other area, delayed, inverted, own reaction) – add the same state again with its settings; the row wins over the function. 3. a device from a function that should not be watched – add a row and untick "Active". 4. a door or window you open while at home (e.g. the bedroom window) – add a row and tick "ignore at home". Tick "inverted" only if a sensor reports the wrong way round (shows "closed" when it is open).

w8rs.text: Devices that the automatic search found by their role are listed here without a tick – tick the ones that should be watched, then their settings appear.

items.title: ignore at home
items.tooltip: Outer skin only: watched in full protection, ignored in perimeter and night protection (e.g. the bedroom window you tilt at night)

wskip10.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w9t.text: All times in seconds. The suggestions suit most homes – press "Use suggestions" if you are unsure.

exitDelayFull.label: Exit delay full protection (s)
exitDelayFull.help: Time to leave the house after switching on full protection. Suggestion: 60 s.

exitDelayPerimeter.label: Exit delay perimeter protection (s)
exitDelayPerimeter.help: You stay inside, so little time is needed. Suggestion: 0–10 s.

entryDelay.label: Entry delay (s)
entryDelay.help: Time to switch off after the "delayed" front door was opened. Suggestion: 30 s.

alarmDuration.label: Alarm duration for lamps and sirens (s, 0 = until acknowledged)
alarmDuration.help: How long lamps blink and sirens sound. 0 = until somebody switches the alarm off. Suggestion: 180 s (many local rules allow 3 minutes).

openCheck.label: Open doors/windows when arming
openCheck.help: What happens when a window is still open while switching on. "Warn" switches on anyway and tells you which one.

armEarlyId.label: Armed at once when this contact closes (e.g. front door)
armEarlyId.help: Optional, may stay empty: the door contact of the front door. As soon as you close it behind you, the system is on at once – no waiting for the exit delay.

wskip11.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w10t.text: At night the alarm system can switch on by itself: only doors and windows are watched, you can move around freely inside. In the morning it switches off again.

w10tx.text: Doors and windows with the tick "ignore at home" are not watched at night.

nightEnabled.label: Yes, switch on night protection by itself every night

wskip12.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w12h.text: Switching the alarm system on and off

w12t.text: You switch the alarm system on and off in the panel (e.g. on the wall tablet or the phone). The following makes it more comfortable and safer.

w12lt.text: The search on the page "What do you have?" may already have filled this in.

lockId.label: State of the lock
lockId.help: The state that shows whether the door is locked, e.g. Nuki: nuki-local.0.<id>.status.lockState

lockValues.label: Values meaning "unlocked/opened"
lockValues.help: Values that mean "unlocked". Nuki: 3, 5, 6 (the search fills them in) – a simple switch: true

presenceArm.label: When nobody is at home
presenceArm.help: Suggestion: full protection – nobody is at home.

presenceDisarm.label: Disarm full protection when somebody comes home

pin.label: PIN (empty = no PIN)
pin.help: Empty = no PIN. With a PIN, only somebody who knows it can switch off in the panel.

wskip13.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w13h.text: How do you want to be told?

w13t.text: Choose how messages reach your phone – Telegram, Pushover, WhatsApp, e-mail … The matching adapter must already be installed and set up in ioBroker. To try it: press "Save" at the bottom first (the assistant stays open), then "Send test message".

w13s.text: The search on the page "What do you have?" may already have filled this in.

w13mh.text: Only messengers that Home Guard supports and that are installed can be chosen; the fields the messenger needs appear in its row. Other messengers can be reached via the ioBroker notification manager.

notifyArmingFailed.label: Not armed because of open windows

notifyReport.label: Report-only sensor triggered (garden gate, letter box …)

speechId.label: State for speech (text is written)
speechId.help: The state that reads text aloud – e.g. for Alexa the state "speak" of the Echo (alexa2.0.Echo-Devices.<id>.Commands.speak).

wskip14.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w14h.text: What else should happen on an alarm?

wizQLamps.label: Yes, lamps should go on or blink on an alarm
wizQLamps.help: Makes the alarm visible from outside and chases intruders away; afterwards the lamps go back as they were.

w14st.text: Leave "Value on/off" empty when it is simply switched on and off. "Runs on": an outside siren best only in full protection, so it does not wake the neighbours when you are at home.

wizQActions.label: Yes, switch something else too (roller shutters, outdoor light, camera …)

w14xt.text: One row per thing. Examples for the event "Alarm": outdoor lights or a socket on, roller shutters up, start a camera recording, the radio loud. With a second row and the event "Alarm ended" you switch it back. Other events, e.g. "Full protection armed": lock the door or roller shutters down. Value: true = on, false = off, a number for roller shutters or dimmers (e.g. 0 or 100). Scenes and scripts work too: the state of the scene, or for a script javascript.0.scriptEnabled.<name> with true.

wskip15.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w15t.text: While you are away, lamps are switched as if somebody were at home: the evening and morning lamps at your times, and in addition short visits to the hall or bathroom and lights out one after the other at bedtime. Which lamps, comes after the times.

simCoupling.label: Runs automatically

options.label: Full protection or nobody at home

simCoupling.help: Recommended: "full protection or nobody at home" – then it also runs when you forgot to switch on.

w15np.text: Without presence detection Home Guard does not know when you are away – choose "When full protection is armed".

w15na.text: Without the alarm system the simulation can only start when nobody is at home – choose "When nobody is at home".

simMode.label: Planning
simMode.help: Recommended: combination. "Learned" means: Home Guard notes on normal days when you switch which lamp, and replays that – it needs a few days for it. Until then it uses random times.

wizSimMorning.label: The simulation should also make light in the morning (at wake-up time)

w15mo.text: In the morning it uses the times and lamps of the morning light.

simVisits.label: Short visits per evening
simVisits.help: Random short visits as long as nothing has been learned yet. 0 = only what was learned.

wskip16.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w16c.text: The evening light is a comfort function for you at home: in the evening the light is simply there, without anybody having to think of it.

w16t.text: In the evening the evening lamps go on around dusk and off at bedtime – every evening with the evening light, while you are away with the simulation. Every time gets a random part, so nobody can see a fixed pattern. Which lamps are evening lamps, you choose afterwards.

simStartRandom.label: Random delay of the start up to (min)
simStartRandom.help: So the lamps do not go on at exactly the same minute every day. Suggestion: 20 min.

simEnd.label: Lights out from (HH:MM)
simEnd.help: When you usually go to bed. Suggestion: 22:30.

simEndRandom.label: Random delay of lights out up to (min)

simWeekendLater.label: Friday/Saturday later by (min)
simWeekendLater.help: On Friday and Saturday evening the lights go out this much later. Suggestion: 45 min.

simLuxId.label: Brightness sensor (optional)
simLuxId.help: The outdoor brightness sensor – on dark days the evening starts earlier, in the morning the lamps go off when it is bright.

simLuxBelow.label: Start earlier when below lux
simLuxBelow.help: Lux = brightness. Around dusk outdoor sensors show about 50–200 lux.

wskip17.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w17c.text: The morning light is a comfort function for you at home: on dark mornings it is already light when you get up.

w17t.text: On dark mornings the morning lamps go on at wake-up time and off again when it is light – every morning with the morning light, while you are away with the simulation. Which lamps are morning lamps, you choose on the next page.

simWake.label: Wake-up time (HH:MM)
simWake.help: When you get up on working days. Suggestion: 06:30.

simWakeRandom.label: Random delay of wake-up up to (min)
simWakeRandom.help: So the lamps do not go on at exactly the same minute every morning. Suggestion: 20 min.

simMorningOffOffset.label: Off: minutes after sunrise
simMorningOffOffset.help: In the morning the lamps go off this long after sunrise. Suggestion: 5 min.

simMorningOffTime.label: Off at the latest at (HH:MM, empty = no)
simMorningOffTime.help: Optional: e.g. when you leave the house – then the lamps go off at the latest at this time (at the weekend later, like the wake-up time).

simMorningLuxAbove.label: Off as soon as brightness above (lux, 0 = no)
simMorningLuxAbove.help: With the brightness sensor: off as soon as it is brighter. 0 = not used.

wskip18.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w18t.text: Each lamp gets one or more roles (ticks in the table): Evening – on from dusk to bedtime. Morning – on at wake-up time. Short visits – hall or bathroom briefly, only during the simulation. Bedtime – briefly on at lights out, only during the simulation. Evening and morning lamps can simply come from a function; all others go into the table.

w18s.text: The search on the page "What do you have?" may already have filled this in.

simAuto.label: Lamps through functions (evening and morning light)

enumMorningLamps.label: Function morning light
enumMorningLamps.hidden: !((data.simEnabled || data.eveningLight || data.morningLight)) || (!data.simAuto || !(data.morningLight || (data.simEnabled && (data.wizSimMorning || (data.simAuto && data.enumMorningLamps) || (data.simLamps || []).some(r => r && r.id && r.morning)))))

w18dt.text: Your TV or radio: add a row with the type "Device / scene / script" – it only runs during the simulation. Best with "Learn from" its real power state, then your real evenings are replayed. A scene (e.g. TV on, then a channel) or a script (javascript.0.scriptEnabled.…) works too.

w18l0h.text: Untick to switch a row off without deleting it. A switched-off row also takes out a lamp that a function (evening or morning light) has found.

w18l1h.text: The data point that switches the lamp or device – e.g. the alias of the lamp (…SET or …ON). Choose the switching data point, not one that only shows a value.

w18l2h.text: How the lamp appears in the plan, in the panel and in the logbook. Empty = the name of the data point.

w18l3h.text: Lamp: switched according to its roles (the next four columns). Device / scene / script: e.g. TV, radio or a scene – runs only while the simulation runs, with its own time window, how often and how long (columns further right).

w18l4h.text: On at dusk, off at lights out – every evening as evening light, also when you are at home, and during the simulation.

w18l5h.text: On at your wake-up time, off a little after sunrise – only while it is still dark.

w18l6h.text: Now and then briefly on and off in the evening – as if somebody went to the hall or the bathroom. Only while the simulation runs.

w18l7h.text: Shortly after lights out briefly on, then off – as if somebody went to bed. Only while the simulation runs.

w18l8h.text: Only if "on" is not simply on: e.g. a dimmer at 80, a scene or a TV channel. Empty = on (or the maximum).

w18l9h.text: Only if "off" is not simply off. Empty = off (or 0).

w18l10h.text: Only if the switching data point does not show whether the lamp or device is really on – e.g. the real power state of the TV. Learned times take precedence over random ones and are learned in the time window of the device.

w18l11h.text: In the evening (dusk to lights out), the whole day (wake-up to lights out) or own times. It only runs while the simulation runs.

w18l12h.text: Only for "own times", e.g. 09:00-20:00 – also over midnight.

w18l13h.text: Per day, a number or a range like 1-3 (random each day). Empty = the general setting "Devices: times per evening".

w18l14h.text: How long each time, e.g. 30-90. Empty = the general settings "Devices run from / to (min)".

w18l15h.text: When you come home: "automatic" switches devices such as the TV off and leaves lamps on, so nobody stands in the dark. Or always switch off, or leave on.

options.label: in the evening (dusk to lights out)
the whole day (wake-up to lights out)

wskip19.text: This page is not needed for your answers – go on with "Next".

w19ah.text: I found Alexa at your place

w19at.text: Your Echo devices can help Home Guard in two ways. Answer the questions below one after the other – every setting is explained. "Apply to the table" then fills the table at the bottom, where you can still change everything per Echo.

wizAlexaAlarm.label: Use the Echos for the alarm (sound and announcement)
wizAlexaAlarm.help: All Echos play a loud sound and read the alarm aloud, every 20 seconds while the alarm runs – as long as your sirens (alarm duration; with 0 until somebody acknowledges or disarms). An Echo is an addition to a real siren, not a replacement: it needs the internet and the Amazon login, and it can be unplugged.

wizEchoAlarmVolume.label: Volume for the alarm (0–100)
wizEchoAlarmVolume.help: 80–100 wakes everybody up. Only the announcement gets this volume – music and radio are not changed.

wizEchoAlarmSound.label: Alarm sound
wizEchoAlarmSound.help: A sound of Amazon's sound library before the announcement. "Alarm" is the most urgent one.

wizEchoAlarmText.label: Read the alarm aloud
wizEchoAlarmText.help: The Echo says what happened, e.g. "Alarm: terrace door" – useful when you are at home at night.

wizAlexaSim.label: Use an Echo for the presence simulation (radio while you are away)
wizAlexaSim.help: One Echo plays radio during the presence simulation, so the house does not sound empty. It only runs while the simulation runs (alarm armed or nobody at home) – never while you are at home.

wizEchoSimDevice.label: Which Echo plays the radio?
wizEchoSimDevice.help: Only Echos with a speaker for music are listed. Best one that can be heard at the front door or from the terrace.

wizEchoStations.label: Station(s)
wizEchoStations.help: The name as you would say it to Alexa, e.g. "Radio Siegen" – or a TuneIn ID like s12345. Several separated by commas: each time a random one, e.g. "Radio Siegen, WDR 2, 1LIVE". Empty = what played last.

wizEchoSimVolume.label: Volume for the radio (0–100)
wizEchoSimVolume.help: So that it can be heard at the door without disturbing the neighbours – about 40–60.

wizEchoWindow.label: When

options.label: in the evening (dusk to lights out)
the whole day (wake-up to lights out)

wizEchoWindow.help: In the evening: dusk to lights out (like the TV). The whole day: from your wake-up time to lights out – radio typically runs in the daytime. Own times: e.g. 09:00-20:00.

wizEchoCount.label: How often per day
wizEchoCount.help: A number, or a range like "1-3" – then a random number each day, so no two days look the same. The runs are spread over the time window and never overlap.

wizEchoDur.label: How long each time (minutes)
wizEchoDur.help: e.g. "30-90" = between half an hour and an hour and a half, random each time.

wizEchoLearn.label: Learn when radio or music really plays
wizEchoLearn.help: Home Guard notes when this Echo really plays (at least 5 minutes – answers to questions, alarms and timers do not count) and replays that instead of random times. Only useful if you listen to radio or music on this Echo regularly.

w19atab.text: Here every Echo has its own row with its own settings for the alarm and the radio – the columns are the same as the questions above. Change a row only if one Echo should behave differently from the others.

items.title: Station(s): name or TuneIn ID, several = random

options.label: in the evening (dusk to lights out)
the whole day (wake-up to lights out)

w19c0.text: Nothing is ticked under "What do you want to use?" – Home Guard has nothing to do.

w19c1.text: ⚠ No sensors – the alarm system cannot raise an alarm. → pages "Outer skin" … "Single sensors & exceptions"
w19c1.hidden: !(data.alarmEnabled && !(data.autoPerimeter && data.enumPerimeter) && !(data.autoFull && data.enumFull) && !(data.autoFire && data.enumFire) && !(data.sensors || []).some(r => r && r.id && r.enabled !== false))

w19c2.text: ⚠ No messenger – when you are away, you will not learn about an alarm. → page "Messages"

w19c3.text: ⚠ A door lock is ticked, but no lock state is chosen. → page "Switching on and off"

w19c4.text: Note: no door is "delayed" and nothing switches off by itself – opening the front door while armed raises the alarm at once. Mark the front door as "delayed" or use the lock or presence. → page "Single sensors & exceptions"

w19c5.text: ⚠ Presence is ticked, but no person is set up. → page "Who lives here?"

w19c6.text: ⚠ The simulation has no lamps. → page "Lamps"

w19c7.text: ⚠ The simulation should start when nobody is at home, but presence is not set up. → page "Simulation: when and how"

w19c8.text: ⚠ Evening light is ticked, but no lamp has the role "Evening". → page "Lamps"
w19c8.hidden: !(data.eveningLight && !(data.simAuto && data.enumSimLamps) && !(data.simLamps || []).some(r => r && r.id && r.enabled !== false && (r.evening || r.type === "evening")))

w19c9.text: ⚠ Morning light is ticked, but no lamp has the role "Morning". → page "Lamps"
w19c9.hidden: !(data.morningLight && !(data.simAuto && data.enumMorningLamps) && !(data.simLamps || []).some(r => r && r.id && r.enabled !== false && (r.morning || r.type === "morning")))

h1.text: Home Guard – alarm system & presence simulation

i1.text: Both parts can be used on their own. Sensors, lamps and persons can be found automatically through functions (enums) or entered by hand.

i2.text: Full protection: all sensors (outer doors, windows and inside). Perimeter protection: only outer doors and windows – you are at home. Night protection: like perimeter protection, armed automatically at night. Danger detectors (smoke, water, gas) report always.

docLink.label: README: widget for AURA, vis-2 and other visualisations, states and script commands

i1.text: All states of the chosen function are monitored. If channels or devices are in the function, their sensor states are taken. The name comes from the description of the object, otherwise from its name.

autoFull.label: Inside sensors (motion detectors …) – full protection only

autoPerimeter.label: Outer skin sensors (doors, windows, glass break …) – full, perimeter and night protection

autoFire.label: Always active (smoke, water, gas, panic button …) – also when disarmed

hazardDefault.label: Reaction of the danger detectors of the function

autoReport.label: Report-only sensors (garden gate, letter box, shed) – a message, never an alarm

reportWhen.label: Report-only sensors report
reportWhen.help: Switch on/off at any time without a restart: state control.report

h2.text: Sensors by hand (a row overrides a sensor found through a function)

srs.text: Devices that the automatic search found by their role are listed here without a tick – tick the ones that should be watched, then their settings appear.

items.title: ignore at home
items.tooltip: Outer skin only: watched in full protection, ignored in perimeter and night protection (e.g. the bedroom window you tilt at night)

iSensors.text: "delayed": entry delay instead of an immediate alarm (the door you come in through). "inverted": the sensor reports open as false. "ignore at home" (outer skin only): watched in full protection, ignored in perimeter and night protection – e.g. the bedroom window you tilt at night.

motionCount.label: Motion detectors: alarm only from this many different detectors
motionCount.help: 1 = every detector at once. 2 or more: a cat or a curtain alone is no alarm.

sabotageHours.label: Report sensors that have not reported for … hours (0 = off)
sabotageHours.help: e.g. empty battery or radio problem

armEarlyId.label: Armed at once when this contact closes (e.g. front door)
armEarlyId.help: Shortens the exit delay: as soon as the door is shut, the system is armed

entryDelay.label: Entry delay (s)
entryDelay.help: For sensors ticked "delayed" (e.g. front door): time to disarm after coming in

alarmDuration.label: Alarm duration for lamps and sirens (s, 0 = until acknowledged)

pinForDisarmState.label: Disarm by state only with the PIN
pinForDisarmState.help: control.mode/control.off do not disarm then – only control.pin, the panel or the lock

maxWrongPin.label: Report after so many wrong entries

pinLockMin.label: Lock the PIN entry afterwards for (min, 0 = no)

lockEnabled.label: Disarm when the lock is unlocked

lockId.label: State of the lock
lockId.help: e.g. Nuki, Danalock, Homematic or any lock with an open/closed state

lockValues.label: Values meaning "unlocked/opened"
lockValues.help: true for locks that only know open/closed – Nuki lockState: 3,5,6 (3 = unlocked, 5 = unlatched, 6 = unlocked lock ’n’ go)

i2.text: A person counts as at home when the state is true (or > 0).

iPersons.text: Several states of one person (e.g. GPS and ping) get the same name: the person counts as at home when one of them says so. States of the function can be named here too. Without a name, the object name without endings like _GPS or _Ping is used.

presenceDisarm.label: Disarm full protection when somebody comes home

nmh.text: Only messengers that Home Guard supports and that are installed can be chosen; the fields the messenger needs appear in its row. Other messengers can be reached via the ioBroker notification manager.

notificationManager.label: Alarm also to the ioBroker notifications (notification manager)

notifyReport.label: Report-only sensor triggered (garden gate, letter box …)

notifyArmingFailed.label: Not armed because of open windows

alarmRepeatMin.label: Repeat the alarm message every minutes until acknowledged (0 = no)

speechId.label: State for speech (text is written)
speechId.help: e.g. alexa2…speak, sayit.0.tts.text or your own text state

iSirens.text: An alarm while disarmed (danger detector, panic) sounds every siren.

i3.text: e.g. lock the door when armed, roller shutters down, camera recording on alarm. Values: true, false, numbers or text.

i4.text: The test switches the ticked parts for real, marked as a test, without arming and without a real alarm. Afterwards lamps go back as before, sirens off and the actions of "Alarm ended" run. Acknowledge ends it early. Save the settings first.

confirm.title: Test alarm
confirm.text: The ticked parts are switched for real now (lamps, sirens, devices) and notifications are sent. Continue?

options.label: Full protection or nobody at home

i1.text: Learning: switching of the simulation lamps that did not come from Home Guard is stored per day. The simulation replays a whole real day with shifted times – the same weekday first, then the same kind of day (weekday/weekend). Without learned days dusk is used.

simAuto.label: Lamps through functions (evening and morning light)

options.label: in the evening (dusk to lights out)
the whole day (wake-up to lights out)

iDevices.text: Type "Device / scene / script": any state that is switched only while the simulation runs – TV, radio, a socket, a scene of the scenes adapter (e.g. TV on, then a channel) or a script (javascript.0.scriptEnabled.…). With "Learn from" (e.g. the real power state of the TV) it replays the real evenings; without, it runs a few times for a random time. "When the simulation ends": automatic switches devices off and leaves lamps on (e.g. coming home). Entries in the table override the ones found through a function.

simJitter.label: Shift learned times randomly by up to ± (min)

simLearnPick.label: Choose learned day
simLearnPick.help: Weekday/weekend: any learned weekday for a weekday evening (Sun–Thu), any Friday/Saturday for the weekend. Same day of the week: a Thursday for a Thursday when at least 3 are learned.

simLearnDevicesOnly.label: Learn only switching by hand/devices (no scripts, scenes)

options.label: when it is dark (from before sunset to sunrise)

iEvening.text: Switches the evening lamps (function "evening light" or "Evening" ticked in the table) every evening, also when somebody is at home: at dusk ALL of them on (also those switched off by hand the evening before), at "lights out" ALL of them off (also those switched on by hand). Times as set under dusk. Short visits, bedtime and learned switching only run while the simulation runs – so nobody at home is surprised by the toilet light at night.

eveningLight.label: Evening light every evening, also when somebody is at home

simStartRandom.label: Random delay of the start up to (min)

simEndRandom.label: Random delay of lights out up to (min)

iMorning.text: Morning lamps (function "morning light" or "Morning" ticked in the table): on at wake-up time, off a little after sunrise – only when it is still dark. Without the morning light they run only while the simulation runs; with it every morning, also when somebody is at home.

morningLight.label: Morning light every morning, also when somebody is at home

simWakeRandom.label: Random delay of wake-up up to (min)

simMorningOffTime.label: Off at the latest at (HH:MM, empty = no)
simMorningOffTime.help: e.g. when you leave the house; later on the weekend like the wake-up time

simMorningLuxAbove.label: Off as soon as brightness above (lux, 0 = no)
simMorningLuxAbove.help: Brightness sensor from the evening section

at.text: Per Echo and per use: on alarm it plays a sound and reads the alarm aloud (as an addition to a real siren – it needs the internet and the Amazon login of the alexa2 adapter); in the presence simulation it plays radio while you are away – a fixed station or a random one of several, in the evening, the whole day or at your own times. With "Learn" Home Guard notes when radio or music really plays (at least 5 minutes; answers to questions do not count) and replays that.

items.title: Station(s): name or TuneIn ID, several = random

options.label: in the evening (dusk to lights out)
the whole day (wake-up to lights out)

al0h.text: All Echos play a loud sound and read the alarm aloud, every 20 seconds while the alarm runs – as long as your sirens (alarm duration; with 0 until somebody acknowledges or disarms). An Echo is an addition to a real siren, not a replacement: it needs the internet and the Amazon login, and it can be unplugged.

al1h.text: 80–100 wakes everybody up. Only the announcement gets this volume – music and radio are not changed.

al2h.text: A sound of Amazon's sound library before the announcement. "Alarm" is the most urgent one.

al3h.text: The Echo says what happened, e.g. "Alarm: terrace door" – useful when you are at home at night.

al4h.text: One Echo plays radio during the presence simulation, so the house does not sound empty. It only runs while the simulation runs (alarm armed or nobody at home) – never while you are at home.

al5t.text: Station(s): name or TuneIn ID, several = random

al5h.text: The name as you would say it to Alexa, e.g. "Radio Siegen" – or a TuneIn ID like s12345. Several separated by commas: each time a random one, e.g. "Radio Siegen, WDR 2, 1LIVE". Empty = what played last.

al6h.text: So that it can be heard at the door without disturbing the neighbours – about 40–60.

al7h.text: In the evening: dusk to lights out (like the TV). The whole day: from your wake-up time to lights out – radio typically runs in the daytime. Own times: e.g. 09:00-20:00.

al9h.text: A number, or a range like "1-3" – then a random number each day, so no two days look the same. The runs are spread over the time window and never overlap.

al10h.text: e.g. "30-90" = between half an hour and an hour and a half, random each time.

al11h.text: Home Guard notes when this Echo really plays (at least 5 minutes – answers to questions, alarms and timers do not count) and replays that instead of random times. Only useful if you listen to radio or music on this Echo regularly.
